chunks: Ahmad ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from some of his companions, raising it (marfu'), said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Foolishness and arrogance cannot exist in the heart of a scholar.

key_terms.السفه: Foolishness, intellectual shallowness, recklessness in judgment
key_terms.العالم: The scholar — one who possesses true religious knowledge
key_terms.الغرة: Heedless arrogance, self-deception, delusion about one's own state

ai.seo_question: Can a true Islamic scholar be foolish or arrogant?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) declares that true scholarship is incompatible with foolishness (safah) and heedless arrogance (ghirra). This hadith reflects the Shia understanding that genuine religious knowledge purifies the heart, making the scholar immune to the vices of shallow thinking and self-deception. The early Muslim audience understood 'scholar' (alim) as one who knows God's commands and lives by them — such a person, by definition, could not harbor ignorance or conceit.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Abdullah, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Barqy, from one of his companions, raising it, said,
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There cannot happen to be the foolishness and the arrogance in the heart of a scholar’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ahmad ibn ‘Abdallah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi from certain persons of his people in a marfu‘ manner (rafa’ahu) from Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Foolishness and arrogance are not found in the hearts of the scholars.”
